evidence.claim: The World Bank projected poverty to rise to 6.6 percent in 2022 as relief measures were phased out amid elevated inflation and said more targeted and cost-effective social assistance was needed.
evidence.title: Thailand's economy is projected to recover to its pre-pandemic level in 2022
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank projected poverty to rise to 6.6 percent in 2022 as relief measures were phased out amid elevated inflation and said more targeted and cost-effective social assistance was needed.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same release, but this is a distinct distributional claim with a clear numerical forecast and policy implication.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 outcomes and late-2022 policy conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Prayut government only in the sense that its fiscal choices shaped the safety net; inflation and commodity shocks also mattered.
contrary_evidence: The passage is a forecast and recommendation, not a direct ruling on government intent or implementation.

evidence.claim: Prayut confirmed he would register with Ruam Thai Sang Chart and run for head of government under that party's banner, after previously remaining non-committal about his political future.
evidence.title: At last, Prayut will run for PM under Ruam Thai Sang Chart banners
evidence.excerpt: Prayut confirmed he would register with Ruam Thai Sang Chart and run for head of government under that party's banner, after previously remaining non-committal about his political future.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting on a late-2022 public confirmation, though from a smaller local outlet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's own political choice.
contrary_evidence: The source is secondary and smaller than Reuters, so it is best used as supportive context rather than a standalone anchor.

evidence.claim: Prayut said he had tried his best, would respect voters' choice, was acting for the benefit of most people, and described the government's work as responding to unprecedented crisis and hardship.
evidence.title: I've done my best, says Prayut
evidence.excerpt: Prayut said he had tried his best, would respect voters' choice, was acting for the benefit of most people, and described the government's work as responding to unprecedented crisis and hardship.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous interview with attributed quotations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's own public framing of his governing purpose.
contrary_evidence: This is self-description, not independent proof of delivery.

evidence.claim: Thailand's parliament passed the first reading of the 3.185 trillion baht budget bill, and Prayut said it would support economic recovery after the crisis and help restore strong and sustained growth.
evidence.title: Thai parliament passes $93 billion budget bill at first reading
evidence.excerpt: Thailand's parliament passed the first reading of the 3.185 trillion baht budget bill, and Prayut said it would support economic recovery after the crisis and help restore strong and sustained growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire story with exact budget figures and an attributed quote from Prayut.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut as prime minister and the cabinet-backed budget process.
contrary_evidence: The first reading shows intent and mobilization, not full implementation or final outcomes.

evidence.claim: The House approved the 3.18-trillion-baht fiscal 2023 budget, which the government said would revive the economy and accelerate its economic master plan and other economic and social development plans.
evidence.title: House approves delayed budget
evidence.excerpt: The House approved the 3.18-trillion-baht fiscal 2023 budget, which the government said would revive the economy and accelerate its economic master plan and other economic and social development plans.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report on a completed budget approval with clear summary of intended use.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Prayut's government because it concerns the budgetary tool he led through parliament.
contrary_evidence: Passing a budget does not itself prove effective execution on the ground.

evidence.claim: Thailand's cabinet approved tax incentives for electric vehicles and skilled foreigners, including lower import duty and excise tax on EVs and a goal of making 30 percent of auto production EVs by 2030.
evidence.title: Thailand approves tax breaks for EVs, high potential foreigners
evidence.excerpt: Thailand's cabinet approved tax incentives for electric vehicles and skilled foreigners, including lower import duty and excise tax on EVs and a goal of making 30 percent of auto production EVs by 2030.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with specific policy measures, targets, and quoted ministerial justification.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Prayut's cabinet and the economic policy line it controlled.
contrary_evidence: The plan is a policy input; the source does not by itself show long-run success.

evidence.claim: The cabinet extended and enlarged the diesel excise-tax cut to 5 baht per litre for two months, and Prayut said the measure was necessary to protect people and manufacturing from higher living costs.
evidence.title: Thailand approves tax cut on diesel to ease high prices
evidence.excerpt: The cabinet extended and enlarged the diesel excise-tax cut to 5 baht per litre for two months, and Prayut said the measure was necessary to protect people and manufacturing from higher living costs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with direct attribution and concrete policy terms.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut as cabinet leader managing the fuel-price response.
contrary_evidence: This is crisis management, not a durable structural reform.

evidence.claim: Thailand aimed for 5 million to 15 million foreign tourist arrivals in 2022 as it eased travel restrictions to support the tourism sector.
evidence.title: Thailand targets 5 million to 15 million foreign tourists this year
evidence.excerpt: Thailand aimed for 5 million to 15 million foreign tourist arrivals in 2022 as it eased travel restrictions to support the tourism sector.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire report with a clear policy objective and sector-specific implementation context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Prayut's government because it concerns easing restrictions and sector revival policy.
contrary_evidence: The article reflects a recovery push, but not whether the target was met.

evidence.claim: Applications for investment promotion in 2022 reached 664.6 billion baht, up 39 percent, and a board meeting chaired by Prime Minister Prayut approved coordination for regional headquarters, renewable energy facilitation, and three large projects.
evidence.title: Thailand 2022 Investment Pledges up 39% to USD20 Billion Helped by FDI flows in Electronics, EV, Data Centers
evidence.excerpt: Applications for investment promotion in 2022 reached 664.6 billion baht, up 39 percent, and a board meeting chaired by Prime Minister Prayut approved coordination for regional headquarters, renewable energy facilitation, and three large projects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official BOI release with quantitative results and explicit PM-chaired approvals.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Prayut's government and its investment-promotion machinery, though not solely to Prayut personally.
contrary_evidence: The release shows a strong year for some sectors, but it does not exclude weaknesses elsewhere or establish durability.

evidence.claim: Thailand expected overall investment applications to fall 22 percent to 500 billion baht in 2022 after a first-half slump, while foreign investment more than halved year on year.
evidence.title: Thailand sees 22% drop in investment pledges this year
evidence.excerpt: Thailand expected overall investment applications to fall 22 percent to 500 billion baht in 2022 after a first-half slump, while foreign investment more than halved year on year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with specific year-on-year figures and policy response context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Prayut government only in a limited sense because the figures also reflect global and sectoral conditions.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes government measures to attract investors later in the year, so the final annual picture was mixed.

evidence.claim: Prayut denied speculation about a cabinet reshuffle, said he would have the final say on the matter, and met coalition figures to press support for the cabinet before the censure vote.
evidence.title: No reshuffle, says defiant PM
evidence.excerpt: Prayut denied speculation about a cabinet reshuffle, said he would have the final say on the matter, and met coalition figures to press support for the cabinet before the censure vote.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous reporting with attributed remarks and coalition detail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut as cabinet leader managing his coalition and ministry lineup.
contrary_evidence: The piece also shows coalition friction and the possibility of deal-making rather than seamless control.

evidence.claim: Prayut appointed Ruam Thai Sang Chart leader Pirapan Salirathavibhaga as his new permanent secretary, and the report says the post supervises the PM Office and coordinates between the prime minister and senior figures.
evidence.title: Prayut appoints Ruam Thai Sang Chart leader as PMs secretary-general
evidence.excerpt: Prayut appointed Ruam Thai Sang Chart leader Pirapan Salirathavibhaga as his new permanent secretary, and the report says the post supervises the PM Office and coordinates between the prime minister and senior figures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report on a concrete appointment to a crucial coordinating post.
evidence.period_fit: Direct target-year appointment and coordination evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's choice of a key aide and the PM Office structure.
contrary_evidence: The appointment may also reflect election positioning, not just administrative competence.

evidence.claim: Prayut announced that he would run as Ruam Thai Sang Chart's prime-ministerial candidate, said he had worked hard for people across Thailand, and said the important thing was to continue the governments work in a sustainable way.
evidence.title: Prayut to run as PM candidate for a new party in the next election
evidence.excerpt: Prayut announced that he would run as Ruam Thai Sang Chart's prime-ministerial candidate, said he had worked hard for people across Thailand, and said the important thing was to continue the governments work in a sustainable way.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct public announcement with attributed quotations.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and relevant to the transition into the next election.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Prayut's own political strategy and revealed goal of continuing in office.
contrary_evidence: This is a campaign statement, so it reveals ambition more than proven administrative success.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 ruler-attributed existential-risk choice, escalation, or crisis-management episode is shown.
Command-and-control, custody, and safety-governance evidence tied specifically to Prayut remains thin.
PM-level attribution for 2022 international-security choices is still thin; most evidence is ministry or delegation posture.
The Myanmar and Ukraine material does not yet show concrete peace or accountability outcomes attributable to Prayut.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for the APEC crackdown and the deep-south emergency regime remains limited.
The torture/disappearance law is an important reform, but year-end enforcement evidence is still weak.
Direct evidence on the sponsors and mechanism of the election-system change is still thin.
4B.4 and 4B.7 remain under-evidenced relative to the stronger protest, media, and term-limit material.
Budget intent and macro recovery are better evidenced than actual implementation and take-up.
Evidence on appointments, anti-capture, and mistake-correction is still weak.
Direct service-delivery, take-up, and quality evidence is thin outside budget allocations and national surveys.
Ruler-specific causal attribution for rural, child, and mental-health outcomes remains weak.
No independent 2022 finding of personal lying, self-dealing, or concealed conflict of interest is shown.
The package relies too much on allegations, self-defense, and broader regime context.
The program basis is only partly explicit; some objectives are inferred from budgets and coalition moves rather than a single frozen program statement.
Outcome evidence is sectoral and mixed, and external reopening effects remain hard to separate from ruler skill.
